title: Space Warfighter Training, Modeling, and Simulation Support
description: I. General Information: The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this Sources Sought or reimburse any costs associated with the preparation of responses. This Sources Sought is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this notice marked "Proprietary" will be handled accordingly. In accordance with RFO 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responses to this Sources Sought will assist the Government in determining the potential level of interest, competition adequacy, and technical capabilities of industry respondents (specifically small businesses) to provide the required products and services. The Government may also use this information to assist in determining whether a small business set-aside (or other socioeconomic set-aside) will be appropriate or developing any subsequent small business subcontract participation and small business goal percentages. The Government does not intend to respond to questions posed in Industry responses. The Government does not guarantee any action beyond this notice. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Responses that are incomplete and/or not submitted per the Response Submission Instructions may not be reviewed. Interested parties or potential contractors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) before the issuance of a potential Request for Proposals/Quotes to be eligible for contract award or payment if the Government chooses to make an award. Information on registration and annual confirmation requirements may be obtained via SAM.gov. Conflict of interest rules apply, and offerors will be required to submit mitigation plans following the release of the RFP. II. Requirement Information: This Sources Sought notice seeks to identify qualified firms capable of providing comprehensive, non-personal mission support services for the 392d Combat Training Squadron (392 CTS). Under this framework, contractor personnel will deliver core capabilities to plan, integrate, execute, and assess Modeling and Simulation (M&S)-enabled exercises (including SPACE FLAG, FLASH POINT, POLARIS HAMMER, and SPACE SKIES) in support of U.S., joint, and allied warfighters. To ensure the continuous readiness of United States Space Force (USSF), joint and coalition forces, this expertise spans a critical array of warfare domains, including Satellite Communications (SATCOM), Global Positioning Systems (GPS), Electronic Attack (EA), Orbital Warfare (OW), Space Electronic Warfare (SEW), Space Domain Awareness (SDA), Missile Warning (MW), and Offensive Cyber Operations (OCO). Furthermore, contractor personnel will drive operational execution by providing Command and Control (C2) support, intelligence product generation, operations assessments, and lessons learned (L2). This operational framework is firmly underpinned by robust technical requirements, encompassing full-scope IT and cybersecurity support, systems engineering, configuration management, orbital analysis, and sophisticated M&S for the Distributed Mission Operations Center-Space (DMOC-S) and BattleLab enclaves. Ultimately, these integrated capabilities will be leveraged to design, plan, execute, and assess USSF service-level exercises and advanced mission-focused training. Support includes programs identified as Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) and Special Access Required (SAR) administered under the enhanced security guidelines/procedures authorized by Department of Defense DODI 5200.01 (DoD Information Security Program and Protection of Sensitive Compartmented Information) and AFI 16-1404 (Air Force Information Security Program). Responses to this announcement are needed to help inform acquisition planning and to identify capable sources. To efficiently and effectively deliver the required supplies/services, it is anticipated that vendors will have specialized experience in large-scale space exercises, complex IT and M&S environments, and managing highly cleared personnel. III. Purpose: The Government is currently considering NAICS Code 541330 (Engineering Services) and Product Service Code (PSC) R425 (Support � Professional: Engineering/Technical) for this requirement. If your firm believes this requirement should be solicited under a different NAICS code or PSC, please include your detailed rationale and supporting market data within your response. This synopsis is encouraging responses from qualified and capable Small Businesses. Firms responding to this Sources Sought must be U.S. owned and must (1) state whether they are a small or large business based on the size standard above; (2) state if they have socioeconomic classification(s) as follows: Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB); section 8(a) small business; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB); Economically-Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB); a Historically Underutilized Business (HUB) Zone small business; Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB);. Small Businesses that are in or are considering Joint Ventures or Mentor Prot�g� Agreements are encouraged to respond to the source sought. Responses from other than small businesses will be reviewed. Note: If the requirement is set aside for small business, the clause RFO 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, will be included in the contract. The data obtained from this notice will assist the Government in understanding the capabilities available in providing advanced space training, exercise execution, and mission rehearsal capabilities. IV. Scope of Anticipated Effort: The 392 CTS provides space combat training through Live, Virtual, & Constructive (LVC) environments to prepare warfighters to achieve and maintain operational dominance in the space domain. The contractor shall provide Mission Support Services, Information Technology, Communications, and Management Support (ITC&MS), and Advisory and Assistance Services (A&AS). The Government anticipates this requirement will consist of an IDIQ ordering period of five years. Work will primarily take place at Schriever SFB, Suffolk, Buckley SFB, Hurlburt Field, Vandenberg SFB, and other designated facilities. V. description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE: Market Research for Specialized Flight Test and Evaluation Training Services Notice ID: FA3002-26-R-0089 NAICS: 611512 (Flight Training) | PSC: U006 (Education/Training - Vocational/Technical) Place of Performance: CONUS DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited. 1. This is a Sources Sought Notice for planning and market research purposes only in accordance with FAR Part 10; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue a solicitation. 2. title: 155mm Artillery Cannister Assembly
description: Description Important Information: This market survey is for informational and planning purposes only and shall NOT be construed as a Request for Proposal; therefore, no contract will be awarded from this announcement or any follow-up information requests. This notice is not to be construed as a commitment by the government for any purpose other than market research. Requirement: The United States (U.S.) Army Contracting Command- Rock Island at Picatinny(ACC-RI-Pica) on behalf of the Office of the Project Manager for Combat Ammunition Systems (PM CAS) both located at Picatinny Arsenal, ACC is conducting market research to identify potential sources within the National Technology Industrial Base , capable of manufacturing and delivering the 155mm Artillery Cannister Assembly (hereafter referred to as �Cannister Assembly�). The Cannister Assembly is made from four components: Payload Canister (4140 steel), Payload Cover (7075 T6 aluminum) Clocking Keys 1 Clocking Keys 2 (AISI S2 tool steel or S7 as alternate). The purpose of this market survey is to obtain potential sources in addition to current producers to deliver Cannister Assemblies at a rate of no less than 450 cannisters per year by October 2027, no less than 1,000 cannisters per year by March 2028, and no less than 10,000 canisters per year by January 2031. 1. Payload Canister -The cannister (SK02662) is approximately 17 inches in length and 5 inches in diameter, requires a smooth surface finish free of any burrs, and a protective coating against environmental corrosion. The cannister shall be subject to dimensional quality controls to ensure proper form, fit, and function. The cannister must be produced from a 4140 steel, with a final hardness of 47 HRC. 2. Payload Cover -The cover (SK02663) is approximately 5 inches in length and are designed to cover a quarter of the curvature of the 5 inch diameter cannister. Each cover requires a smooth surface finish free of any burrs, and a protective coating against environmental corrosion. The cannister shall be subject to dimensional quality controls to ensure proper form, fit, and function. The cannister must be produced from a 7075 T6 aluminum. There are no limitations on the manufacturing method to achieve the 7075 T6 properties. 3. Clocking Keys 1- The key 1 (SK02665) is approximately 1 inch in length, 0.5 inches wide, and 0.2 inches in depth. It requires a smooth surface finish free of any burrs, and a protective coating by electrodeposited zinc with supplemental chromate treatment, ASTM B644, classification no. Fe/Zn 12. service condition SC3 (severe), Type I I, color olive drab. The key 1 shall be subject to dimensional quality controls to ensure proper form, fit, and function. Dimensional requirements and tolerances shall apply after plating. The key 1 must be produced from a AISI S2 tool steel or S7 as alternate, with a final hardness of 53 HRC. 4. Clocking Keys 2- The key 2 (SK02666) is approximately 0.5 inch in length, 0.5 inches wide, and 0.2 inches in depth. It requires a smooth surface finish free of any burrs, and a protective coating by electrodeposited zinc with supplemental chromate treatment, ASTM B644, classification no. Fe/Zn 12. service condition SC3 (severe), Type I I, color olive drab. The key 2 shall be subject to dimensional quality controls to ensure proper form, fit, and function. Dimensional requirements and tolerances shall apply after plating. The key 2 must be produced from a AISI S2 tool steel or S7 as alternate, with a final hardness of 53 HRC. All interested sources must be registered in the System for Award Management in order to provide a response. Responses shall include the following information for the Government�s review and assessment: a. Company's contact information including organization�s name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, business size, taxpayer identification number, Unique Entity ID and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code (as applicable); b. A summary that includes a brief description of the contractor's capabilities to include: parent organizations, name/address/point of contact identification/email address, website, potential partnering/teaming arrangements, and manufacturing capabilities to include machining, forging, heat treatment, non-destructive testing, and protective coatings. c. Past manufacturing experience with artillery metal parts, cannister assemblies (155mm) or similar scope(s) of work within the last 10 years; d. A description of facilities/equipment, manufacturing processes, inspection capability, personnel, and Quality Management System certifications or standards used. All containers must be affixed with a nameplate that includes a Unique Identification (UID) marking as referenced in the drawing package Drawing ;(80132) 15930; and IAW Mil-STD-130 latest revision. The contractor shall contact NAVICP code ;N241.17; or code 0771.10 for the alphanumeric sequential serial number group that makes up part of the UID. The UIDwill be included on the nameplate in data matrix format. 3.3 Welding and welder qualifications shall be in accordance with AWS D1.1 for steel, AWS D1.2 or MIL-W-22248,Class 4 for aluminum, AWS D1.3 for sheet steel and AWS D1.6 for stainless steel. Proper controls shall be used to prevent melt through or burn through. For aluminum, filler for welding 6061 alloy shall be 4043: filler for welding 5000 series alloys to themselves or to 6061 shall be 5356 or 5556. In addition,welding and weld inspection shall include: (1) Visual inspection shall include 5X (5power) magnification when a suspect condition is to be examined beyond the capability of normal vision. (2) Critical and major welds may be subjected to further non destructive testing (such as dye penetrant inspection)as prescribed by the buying activity. (3) Proper documentation shall be available for review by Government personnel. 3.4 WORK INSTRUCTIONS. Work instructions shall be posted at theoperator's work station giving procedures to control the welding process, i.e., filler material, weld size, electrical and gas characteristics, including flow rate. 3.5 MATERIALS AND MATERIALS CONTROL. The quality program shall assure that the materials used in fabrication or processing, i.e., base metals and weld filler material, be inspected and conform to the applicable physical, chemical and other technical requirements (supplier's certification is sufficient). 3.6 CONTROLS. Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.7 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.8 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.8.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.8.2 MECHANICAL MEANS. Immediately prior to welding, mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied to the weld areas previously chemically treated to assure removal of residual or reformed oxides, if any. Acceptable methods of mechanical cleaning include stainless steel wire brushing, scraping, filing, or sanding. However, abrasives containing iron and its oxides, steel wool and wire, and copper alloy based wire, which may become embedded with galvanically active metals and accelerate corrosion of aluminum alloys shall NOT be used. Mechanical methods shall be vigorous enough to adequately remove any residual oxide films, but gentle enough to avoid forming an excessively rough surface in the comparatively soft metal underneath

description: Sources Sought Notice Description SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS Job Order Contract for Fort Leonard Wood, MO This is a Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) ONLY. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, bids or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this sources sought synopsis. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, IFB, or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Government wide Point of Entry (GPE). It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the GPE for additional information pertaining to this requirement. The GPE is located at https://sam.gov. The United States (U.S.) Government desires to procure a Job Order Contract (JOC) at Fort Leonard Wood, on a small business set-aside basis, provided 2 or more qualified small businesses respond to this sources sought synopsis with information sufficient to support a set-aside. Be advised that the U.S. Government will not be able to set aside this requirement if two (2) or more small businesses do not respond with information to support the set-aside. We encourage all small businesses, in all socioeconomic categories (including, 8(a) Business Development Program, Small Disadvantage Business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned Small Business concerns), to identify their capabilities in meeting the requirement at a fair market price. BACKGROUND: A continuing need is anticipated for a job order contract at Fort Leonard Wood. Attached you will find the draft Statement of Work (SOW). The Government currently contracts for these services under contract W911S723D0001. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and construction services as defined in this SOW. The NAICS code for the requirement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction with a corresponding size standard of $45 million. If your company believes a different NAICS code would better fit this requirement, please tell us your suggested NAICS and why it would better fit this requirement. The Contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, personnel, equipment, materials, and supplies, with the exception of Government Furnished Property (GFP), to perform activities under this Job Order Contract. PURPOSE OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT: To request information on capabilities of potential offerors to provide the services described herein. Electronic submissions only: Responses are due no later than 13:00pm CDT on 8 October 2026 to facilitate planning and ensure maximum consideration. The email attachments cannot exceed 9 megabytes (MB) due to the Government�s email system restrictions. DO NOT SEND ZIPPED files as the Government�s network will remove all zipped files. Interested businesses should provide a brief capability statement package (limited to no more than 30 pages, single spaced, and 12 font size minimum) demonstrating specific capability in reference to this requirement. The Government prefers that your firm submits its response in Microsoft Word, Adobe Acrobat, or a combination of the two and the document(s) must be searchable. Include: Whether the experience has been as a prime contractor or subcontractor on similar requirements (include the services provided, the number of facilities involved, and any other relevant information you deem applicable). Email the capability package to: Ms. Marissa Joyner - Contract Specialist at email: Marissa.joyner.civ@army.mil and Mr. Andrew Graham - Contracting Officer at email: Andrew.s.graham6.civ@army.mil The email subject line should include: The Firm�s Name, �Response to the Sources Sought Synopsis for the JOC at Fort Leonard Wood, W5168W27RA007". **Note: the location(s) and corresponding solicitation number that you are responding to must be identified on the subject line. In response to this sources sought, please provide: 1. A company�s profile must include: The name of the firm, point of contact, phone number, email address, number of employees, annual revenue history, CAGE code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). number. Respondents must also indicate small business certification status, for example: Small Business (SB), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), 8(a), Economically Disadvantaged Woman Owned SB (EDWOSB), WOSB, HUBZone, or Service Disabled Veteran Owned SB (SDVOSB). 2. In essence, what primary tasks should be used for determining minimum capability to provide these services? 3. Whether your firm is interested in competing for this requirement as a prime contractor. If you are subcontracting any of the services out, contemplating a Joint Venture, and/or creating a teaming arrangement, please provide the name of these companies and what work they will be performing, if available. Please provide your company�s specific experience in job order contracts and providing comparable services. Ensure the information is in sufficiently detailed regarding previous experience in managing job order contracts (indicate whether the experience has been as a prime contractor or subcontractor) on similar requirements (include the services provided, the number of facilities involved, and any other relevant information you deem applicable). If applicable, please provide the same experience information from any subcontracts, Joint Venture, and/or teaming partners you may propose with. 4. What percentage of work will be performed by the small business prime contractor and all similarly situated entity subcontractors? Note: In accordance with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (Oct 2022) and Class Deviation 2021-O0008, Revision 1 - Limitations on Subcontracting for Small Business (Feb 2023), for general construction under NAICS 236220, prime contractor and similarly situated subcontractors must perform at least 15% of the cost of the contract, excluding the cost of materials. 5. Type(s)/certifications(s) of proposed subcontractors (for example, SDB, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB). 6. Information on the financial capacity of your business to meet financial obligations (i.e. payroll, payment of subcontractors, etc.). 7. How the Army can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition by and among small business concerns. 8. Identify any condition or action that may have the effect of unnecessarily restricting competition with respect to this acquisition. Please contact the MICC Advocate for Competition, Scott Kukes at email: scott.d.kukes.civ@army.mil or 210-466-3015, if you believe that this action is unreasonably restricting competition. title: HH-60W Degraded Visual Environment System(DVES) - FA8552-26-R-B001
description: Description of Anticipated Requirement: The United States Air Force (USAF) has a need to field a system capable of addressing the issues posed by Degraded Visual Environments (DVE). The HH-60W DVES solution shall provide real-time hazard detection in both enroute and terminal areas, displaying this information clearly on cockpit and cabin displays. It shall be designed to function effectively in a variety of DVE, including those created by ambient/aritificial conditions such as smoke, smog, snow, night sand/dust, etc and aircraft-induced conditions such as brownout/whiteout. This effort will consist of the material solution and all non-recurring engineering required to install a DVE solution on to the HH-60W Jolly Green II helicopter, including the design, development, testing, integration, procurement, installation, and deployment of the DVES kits. Anticipated Contract Period of Performance: One (1) base period of twenty-four (24) months with One (1) Ordering Period and One (1) Option to turn on Ordering Periods 2-6. This establishes an total potential period of performance of eight (8) years.

title: Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) � Anesthesia Workstation System (AWS) Prototype
description: 1.0 Overview The U.S. Army Contracting Command (ACC), on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maneuver Ground, Project Manager Maneuver Medical Systems (PM M2S), is issuing this Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) to solicit prototype project proposals for a modernized Anesthesia Workstation System (AWS). This RPP is issued pursuant to the Other Transaction Authority (OTA) under 10 U.S.C. � 4022. This is a DIRECT OTA and is NOT a solicitation for a procurement contract under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). Consortium membership is not required to respond to this RPP. 2.0 Mission Need & Scope The U.S. Army requires a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) or Non-Developmental Item (NDI) anesthesia workstation system capable of supporting life-saving medical operations in austere environments at Role of Care (ROC) 3 with little to no modification. The system must overcome the capability gaps of legacy systems, specifically regarding interoperability with Army Oxygen Generation Systems, heavy logistical footprint (weight), and proprietary maintenance constraints. The Government intends to award one (1) OT Agreement for the delivery of two (2) prototype units. These units will undergo rigorous operational testing by the Medical Test and Evaluation Activity (MTEAC) and environmental testing conducted in accordance with MIL-STD-810H. Proposed solutions must be FDA-cleared for human use and Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliant. A high priority for this effort is organic supportability. The Government strongly prefers systems designed to be maintainable by military Biomedical Equipment Technicians (BMETs) at the Field and Depot levels without reliance on proprietary vendor service contracts. 3.0 Follow-On Production Authority In accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022(f), this OT Agreement is issued with a provision for follow-on production. Upon successful prototype completion and validation, the Government may award a follow-on production contract or OT Agreement for approximately one hundred and eighty (180) AWS units without further competitive procedures. 4.0 Proposal Submission Instructions All proposal instructions, technical specifications (CODS and APAs), and evaluation criteria are detailed in the attached Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) document. Questions: All questions must be submitted in writing via email to the Agreements Officer and Agreements Specialist no later than 15:00 ET on 17 September 2026. Proposals: Proposals must be submitted via DoD SAFE file transfer or secure email no later than 16:00 ET on 01 October 2026. Communications: Unauthorized contact with program office personnel or technical end-users regarding this RPP may result in disqualification. All communications must be directed to the points of contact listed below. title: Intelligence Exploitation and Targeting Systems (IETS)
description: The purpose this Amendment 1 is to update Attachment 5 L-4 RFP Questions and Responses to respond to industry's questions and concerns. Questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted via email to the contract specialist at aretha.y.jones.civ@us.navy.mil and luke.s.kelley.civ@use.navy.mil utilizing Attachment L-4 RFP Questions Form. Each question or comment should reference the applicable document, page number, and paragraph number.? Offerors shall not include any proprietary information in a question, because the Government will provide the question and answer to all potential offerors. All questions must be submitted no later than 1:00PM Pacific Time on the 7th calendar day after the date that this amendment is issued. Questions received after the deadline above may be answered at the Government�s sole discretion. The Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division at China Lake, CA is soliciting for an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Contract (MAC) on a full and open competitive basis for the development and fielding of Development and Fielding of Intelligence Exploitation and Targeting Systems (IETS) systems/prototypes related to future systems and the sustainment of deployed systems. This is a follow-on effort to IDIQ contracts N6893621D-0016 through -0018. The sources sought for this procurement was posted under solicitation N6893625R0030. This requirement will focus on the continued delivery and fielding of IETS that are based upon or derived from the Common Geo-Positioning (CGS) package of software and related hardware components deployed in the Distributed Common Ground System Navy (DCGS) family of programs. This solicitation is being solicited through the Solicitation Module of the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) at https://piee.eb.mil. All submissions in response to this solicitation must be received in the PIEE Solicitation Module, according to the guidance in the Request for Proposals (RFP). Contractors must be certified through Defense Logistics Information Services (DLIS) in order to access Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) or Export Controlled Information. Access to CUI is limited, to a single point of contact (POC) per CAGE code, who is listed as the Data Custodian on the DD 2345 and approved by Defense Logistics Agency (DLA). The DD 2345 must be approved prior to requesting access to CUI in SAM.gov. Contractors are responsible for coordinating with their CAGE code Data Custodian POC to request access to CUI. For additional information, visit the DLA website for the Joint Certification Program: https://www.dla.mil/HQ/LogisticsOperations/Services/JCP/.

description: This is a combined Sources Sought/Request for Information (RFI) notice. Any information submitted by respondents to this request is strictly voluntary. All information received from this Sources Sought/RFI notice will be used for planning and market research purposes only. The United States (U.S.) Government will treat your response to this Sources Sought/RFI notice as information. Based on the review of responses to this Sources Sought/RFI notice, the Government may elect to release a formal Request for Proposal (RFP) at a future date. The Period of Performance (PoP) for any subsequent contract effort will remain variable and dependent upon the maturity and deployment timelines of the offered solutions. Under any future resultant contract, the prime contractor will be required to execute a comprehensive modernization effort, to include the delivery of all required radar equipment, provision of initial spares, and the execution of all necessary site modifications and system integration. 3.0 Desired Capabilities The below capabilities integrate specific parameters required by the Brazilian Air Force. 3.1 General System must demonstrate the capability to achieve full flight inspection certification (FAA/ICAO standards) for both Airport Surveillance Radar (ASR) and Precision Approach Radar (PAR) functions. 3.2 Transportation a. (O): Full support for all Threshold modes plus native cryptographic integration for secure military Mode 5 e. SSR Probability of Detection (Pd) (T): 90% or higher. (O): 95% or higher. 3.3.2 Precision Landing a. PAR Coverage & Switch Time (T): Service up to 6 runways, switchable within 60 seconds. (O): Service > 6 runways, switchable in under 30 seconds. b. PAR Instrumented Range (T): Reliable azimuth/elevation tracking and detection out to a minimum range of 10 NM. (O): Reliable azimuth/elevation tracking and detection out to 20 NM or greater. c. PAR Target Capacity (T): Track up to 50 aircraft in azimuth and 22 aircraft in elevation. (O): Track over 100 combined aircraft simultaneously. d. PAR Detection Probability (2m� target) (T): 90% probability at 10 NM. (O): 95% probability at 15 NM in rain and 20 NM in clear weather. e. PAR Resolution (T): Range: 400 ft, Azimuth: 1.2 degrees, Elevation: 0.6 degrees (all with greater than or equal to 80% probability). (O): Margins improved by 20% over threshold values. f. PAR Accuracy (T): Range: less than or equal to �100 ft (or 2%). Azimuth: less than or equal to �30 ft. Elevation: less than or equal �20 ft. (O): Margins improved by 20% over threshold values. 3.3.3 Communications Data Interoperability (T=O): Output standard ASTERIX Eurocontrol data format for all surveillance outputs. ATC Positions, Display, & Automation (T): Two (2) ATC positions. Explain and provide detailed documentation of the proposed a. ATC automation/display system. (O): Fully modular system expandable up to six (6) ATC positions. ATC Radio Communications (T): Each ATC position must have UHF/VHF transmit/receive capability and the ability to simultaneously monitor UHF/VHF Guard frequencies. (O): Fully integrated voice switch system with secure, encrypted transmit/receive capability. 3.3.4 System Reliability & Redundancy (T=O): Backup PSR transmitter or redundancy in the system is required. Backup power (UPS) is required. Mean Time Between Critical Failure (MTBCF) > 2,000 hours. 3.3.5 Maintainability (MTTR) (T): Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) < 30 minutes. (O): Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) < 15 minutes. 3.3.6 System Operational Certifications Identify whether or not the system has any/all of six (6) certifications for operations in both CONUS and OCONUS: Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon System (ATCRBS) Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) Mark XII System (AIMS); Cybersecurity; Interoperability and Supportability (I&S); National Airspace System (NAS); Spectrum; and Transportability (air, ground and sea). 3.3.7 Ancillary & Support Equipment Requirements (T): Identify all generators, environmental control unit (ECU), hardware/software, and ancillary equipment requirements necessary to support standalone system operations. title: Encroachment Management Implementation and Mission Readiness, Sustainment, and Compatibility Services AE IDIQ, Unrestricted
description: THIS IS AN UNRESTRICTED PROCUREMENT. This procurement will result in one Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for multi-discipline Architect-Engineer (A-E) services for Encroachment Management Implementation and Mission Readiness, Sustainment, and Compatibility services at various Navy and Marine Corps installations primarily in the Navy Region Southwest but may also include work worldwide. These services will be procured in accordance with 40 USC Chapter 11, Selection of Architects and Engineers, as implemented by FAR 36. The IDIQ contract will be for a base period of two (2) years and three (3) one-year option periods (if exercised). The total fee for the contract term shall not exceed $30,000,000. The guaranteed minimum for the contract term (including option years) is $1,000. Firm-fixed price task orders will be negotiated for this contract. The minimum value of individual task orders executed under this contract is $25,000. The maximum value of individual task orders executed under this contract is $2,500,000. There will be no dollar limit per year. Estimated start date is March 2027. The Small Business size standard classification is North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code 541330 (Engineering Services). The Government seeks the most highly qualified firm to perform the required services, based on the demonstrated competence and qualifications, in accordance with the selection criteria. Primary A-E Services: 1. Land Use Planning. 2. Air Installations Compatible Use Zones (AICUZ) and Range Air Installations Compatible Use Zones (RAICUZ) Studies. 3. Encroachment Action Plans (EAP) or Encroachment Control Plans (ECP). 4. Strategic Engagement and Communication Plans (SECP). 5. Outreach Planning Materials. 6. Electronic Database. Secondary Services: 1. Other related studies/analysis: Provide additional services to assist in implementation of encroachment management studies, Range Complex Management Plans (RCMP), Integrated Natural Resource Management Plans (INRMP), Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration (REPI) Program plans, and other special planning, engineering, and encroachment support deliverables, such as analytical assessments, geospatial analysis and simulations, traffic studies, glint/glare analysis, radar assessments, plume analysis and modeling, lighting studies, and socio-economic studies. 2. Other Related Reports or Documentation: Deliverables also include assistance with incidental services related to providing public notice for studies and publicizing and providing training on encroachment-related studies. Please see attached synopsis for full synopsis description/instructions.

description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THERE WILL NOT BE A SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center (NAVFAC EXWC) is conducting market research and seeking sources for an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Hybrid Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) Single Award Contract; for ARCHITECTURAL-ENGINEER (A/E) services to be conducted worldwide. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 541330 � Engineering Services, and the annual size standard is $25,500,000.00. Forthcoming RFP format will be an SF330. All businesses, including small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owed small businesses, Veteran Owned small businesses, certified HUB-Zone small businesses, certified 8(a) concerns, Woman-Owned Small, and large businesses are encouraged to respond. The information received will be used to formulate the strategy for establishing a set-aside or reserve for small business categories. NAVFAC EXWC anticipates awarding one (1) contract. The aggregate value of all Task Orders issued under the contract resulting from this solicitation shall not exceed $150,000,000 over the sixty-month ordering period, and the four (4) one-year options, if exercised. Multiple Task Orders may be awarded with similar delivery schedules requiring the selected firm to provide services with overlapping work/delivery dates. Individual Task Orders can range between $100,000 and $6,000,000, with obligated amounts per order anticipated to range between $125,000 to $5,900,000. The current contract (N3943022D2400) was awarded to a Joint-Venture business as a Single-Award IDIQ FFP/CPFF Services Contract for similar environmental services, worldwide. The task orders that were within the scope of this predecessor A/E contract had over sixty individual awards as of the date of this posting, with obligated amounts per-order ranging between $20,000 to $4,850,000; for reference, the median award was approximately between $550,000.00 and $600,000. This contract provides engineering and design services, particularly in environmental restoration, as well as in other environmental areas to support U.S. Navy, Marine Corps, and Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) installations and other federal organizations at various locations, worldwide. The draft scope of Architect and Engineering Services is included as an attachment. It is requested that interested businesses submit to the contracting office a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 10 pages in length, single spaced, 12-point font minimum, 10-point font is acceptable for tables and figures) demonstrating ability to perform the requested services. This documentation shall address, at a minimum, the following: (1) Relevant Experience to include experience in performing efforts of similar scope and complexity within the last five years. (2) Company Profile to include number of employees, office locations(s), DUNS number, CAGE Code, and statement regarding small business designation and status. (3) Professional registrations in all states and overseas areas where your company is registered to do work. Incumbent firms need not submit a capabilities statement package. Note that in the forthcoming solicitation, pricing will not be a selection factor. Questions regarding this sources sought notice and capabilities packages may be sent via email to ryan.j.kenniff.civ@us.navy.mil

title: Udbud af revisionsydelser
description: Udbuddet omfatter revision af Kommunen i henhold til kommunestyrelovens § 42 i form af lovpligtig revision og diverse tillægsydelser med begyndelse fra og med regnskabsåret 2027. Kommunen og dens forhold er beskrevet på Kommunens hjemmeside www.htk.dk, hvortil henvises for yderligere information herom. Til belysning af Kommunens revision og regnskaber henvises til Kommunens årsregnskab for 2026 med tilhørende tiltrædelsesberetning, jf. udbudsmaterialets bilag 5 – 6. En oversigt over betalinger til BDO Statsautoriseret Revisionspartnerselskab i årene 2024, 2025 og 2026 (til dato) fremgår af udbudsmaterialets bilag 14. Kommunens krav til revisionsydelserne fremgår af kravspecifikationen og Kommunens opgavebeskrivelse, jf. udbudsmaterialets bilag 2 – 3, og de ydelser, som Kommunen stiller til rådighed for revisor, er specificeret i udbudsmaterialets bilag 3. title: Germany – Construction work for swimming pool – Sorpesee GmbH - Energetische Sanierung Hallenbad Sundern | Holz BHKW
description: Die Sorpesee GmbH beabsichtig, das Hallenbad in Sundern energetisch zu sanieren. Bei dem Gebäude handelt es sich um ein 1-geschossigen, teilweise (ca. 70%) unterkellerten Bau in massiver Bauart. Die Dachkonstruktion über dem Erdgeschoss ist in Holzbauweise (Binder) erstellt worden. Diese wurde als Pultdach (oberhalb der Schwimmhalle) und als Flachdach konzipiert. Oberhalb der Schwimmhalle befindet sich lediglich ein Revisionsgang zur Kontrolle der dort verbauten Lüftungstechnik. Unterhalb des Erdgeschosses allerdings sind ca. 70 % der Flächen unterkellert. Dort befindet sich die Heizungstechnik. Der Keller ist unbeheizt. • Bruttorauminhalt: 21.183 m³ • Bruttogrundfläche Erdgeschoss: 2.113 m² • Bruttogrundfläche Kellergeschoss : 1.304 m² • Nettogrundfläche nach DIN : 3.199 m² Im Vordergrund des Gebäudes und der Nutzung steht die Schwimmhalle selbst. Diese Halle besitzt eine Fläche von ca. 1.083 m². Bei der Bauaufgabe handelt es sich um die Modernisierung und energetische Sanierung des Hallenbads in Sundern sowohl der Fassade, des Daches, der inneren abgehängten Decke und Wandbekleidung als auch der Energieversorgung. Das Hallenbad aus dem Jahr 1975/76 bietet drei Schwimmbecken: ein 25 m langes Schwimmbecken mit höhenverstellbarem Boden, ein Springbecken mit einem 1- Meter, 3- Meter und 5-Meter Sprungturm sowie ein Kinderbecken. Das Hallenbad in Sundern liegt in der Berliner Straße 62 in 59846 Sundern. Vorliegend handelt es sich um Arbeiten zur die Erstellung einer pelletbetriebenen KWK Anlage mit einer Pelletkessel-Kaskade als zusätzliche Heizung für die Gebäudeheizung. Für die Beheizung des Gebäudes steht derzeit ein Gasbrennwertkessel und ein Gas BHKW bereit, diese verbleiben als Notkessel am Aufstellort. Dual zu dem Bestand wird im Nachbarraum die neue pelletbetriebene Heizungsanlage aufgebaut werden.

description: Die Hanse- und Universitätsstadt Rostock, Tiefbauamt, plant den Ersatzneubau der Vorpommernbrücke (BW 102) im Zuge der L 22 über die Warnow. Im Ergebnis einer Machbarkeitsstudie wurde eine Vorzugsvariante entwickelt, die eine Warnowquerung aus 2 Teilbauwerken festlegt. In diesem Zuge sind die Verkehrsanlagen auf dem Bauwerk selbst sowie die auf beiden Seiten vorgelagerten Streckenabschnitte bis zu den Anschlussknoten West und Ost zu planen und zu erneuern. Dabei sind sowohl 2 KFZ- Fahrstreifen stadteinwärts und 2 KFZ- Fahrstreifen stadtauswärts als auch beidseitige Geh- und Radwege zu berücksichtigen. Die vorgesehene Planung der Maßnahme gliedert sich thematisch im Wesentlichen in 3 Teile: 1. die Planung eines neuen Teilbauwerkes Nord (ggf. zzgl. Moorbrücken Nord) mit den entsprechenden verkehrlichen Anbindungen an die benachbarten Knoten, 2. die Planung des Abbruches der Bestandsbauwerke (Vorpommernbrücke, Moorbrücken, Verkehrszeichenbrücke), 3. die Planung eines neuen Teilbauwerkes Süd (ggf. zzgl. Moorbrücken Süd) einschließlich der Planung einer Verkehrszeichenbrücke mit den entsprechenden verkehrlichen Anbindungen an die benachbarten Knoten. Im Rahmen des Vorhabens sind die umweltfachlichen Anforderungen aus Natur-, Arten-, Gewässer-, Boden-, Klima- und Immissionsschutz einschließlich aller daraus resultierenden Genehmigungs- und Nebenbestimmungen zu berücksichtigen.

title: USACE SPK MOTCO Facilities and Utilities Maintenance Services - Concord, California
description: This Sources Sought Notice is being issued for market research purposes to determine the availability, capability, and interest of 8(a) small business firms for a potential Government requirement which the Government intends to compete as a competitive 8(a). NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE. Requests for the solicitation will go unanswered. No award will be made from this Notice. Responses will be used to determine potential acquisition strategies, understand current market capabilities, and to gain knowledge of potential sources. GENERAL SCOPE:The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) anticipates a potential requirement for facilities and utilities maintenance services at U.S. Army Military Ocean Terminal Concord (MOTCO) in Concord, California. USACE SPKs intent is to solicit and award a competitive 8(a) small business requirement.Project Description: This is a non-personal services project to provide Facilities and Utilities Maintenance at U.S. Army Military Ocean Terminal Concord (MOTCO) across the following functional areas: Maintenance Management Services, Electrical Plants and Distribution Systems, Water Distribution Systems, Wastewater Systems, Stormwater Systems, Fire Protection Systems, Buildings and Structures and Installed Equipment, Pest Management, Roads and paved surfaces, Pier Maintenance and various miscellaneous maintenance requirements, and repair requirements including minor construction in accordance with the Performance Work Statement. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, other items, and non-personal services. The Contractor is fully responsible for provisioning all parts required to execute both Preventive Maintenance Orders (PMOs) and Demand Maintenance Orders (DMOs). The potential requirement may result in a firm-fixed-price solicitation with a 6-month or 12-month to include one month Phase-in Period for the base period with four 1-year option periods. The Government intends to issue the solicitation on or around November 2026. If solicited, the Government intends to award the anticipated requirement by approximately June 2027. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for the potential requirement is anticipated to be 561210, Facilities Support Services. The small business size standard for the NAICS, as established by the U.S. Small Business Administration, is $47,000,000 annual revenue. The Product Service Code for the potential requirement is anticipated to be M1AZ, Operation of Other Administrative Facilities and Service Buildings.Contractors with the skill, capabilities, workload capacity, and ability to obtain bonding to complete the project described above (either through self-performance and/or Subcontractor management) are invited to provide capability statements to the primary point of contact listed below. Other than small businesses are also encouraged to submit Capability Statements.CAPABILITY STATEMENT:Industry is highly encouraged to fill out the market survey form at: MOTCO Facilities and Utilities Maintenance Services - Prefilled formResponses will not be considered an offer, proposal, or bid for any solicitation that may result from this Notice. Moreover, responses will not restrict the Government to an acquisition approach. This Notice is for information and planning purposes only. Respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted or the capability statements received. Please provide responses with the above link or submit questions by e-mail to the Contract Specialist, Melita Doyle, at (Melita.S.Doyle@usace.army.mil) by 1400 / 2:00 P.M. (Pacific Time) 08 October 2026. Please include the Sources Sought Notice number W9123826X1CDK in the e-mail subject line.

title: MABSM Sustainment & Implementation Services Sources Sought
description: Notice: This is not a solicitation but rather a Sources Sought Synopsis to determine potential sources for information and planning purposes only. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to determine if responsible sources exist, to assist in determining if this effort can be competitive and/or a total Small Business Set-Aside. PLEASE SEE ADDITIONAL ATTACHMENTS FOR FURTHER DETAILS AND VENDOR CAPABILITY QUESTIONS Program Details: The MABSM application is a highly customized, mission-critical Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) system. Originally built on a baseline commercial Impresa MRO/ERP software foundation, the system has undergone extensive, continuous customization over the past 24 years. To date, the MABSM baseline includes over 242,000 custom code changes, program specifications, testing criteria, and complex interface logic. These modifications enable real-time communication with 17 legacy Department of Defense (DoD) systems. This highly specialized, proprietary configuration of the COTS software bears little structural resemblance to its commercial progenitor and operates as a unique hybrid system. MABSM operates and is sustained within the Department of the Air Force's Cloud 1 enterprise cloud environment, leveraging DoD Impact Level 4/5 (IL4/IL5) secure cloud infrastructure. Sourcing specialized contractors who can operate seamlessly within Cloud 1's DevSecOps frameworks, managed services, and security boundaries is crucial to system stability. MABSM dictates the real-time tracking of critical assets, including aircraft parts, financial transactions, and Nuclear Weapons-Related Material (NWRM) items. Due to the high-tempo depot environments in which it is deployed, the system requires a performance baseline exceeding 95% system uptime and near-zero code degradation. Furthermore, national security mandates dictate 100% real-time accountability of NWRM items within any given 24-hour period. Instructions: The Government requests interested parties provide the following information (please limit your response to no more than 10 pages): Company Name and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code. Name, phone number, and email address for point of contact(s). The applicable NAICS Code for this acquisition is _______. Based on this NAICS Code, what is your size status? ______ Small Business ______ Small Disadvantaged ______ Women-Owned ______ Veteran-Owned ______ Service-Disabled Veteran Owned ______ Hub-Zone ______ 8(a) ______ Large Business Are you currently registered in SAM.gov and WAWF? The NAICS Code selected for this potential requirement is 541513 or 541519, which has a size standard of $37M or $24M. If you disagree that 541513 or 541519 is the proper NAICS Code, please submit that comment to the requiring activity along with what NAICS Code you believe this should be classified under; however, please do not wait for an amendment to this request. The due date for the market survey will remain at 08 October 2026. This date will not be extended. Provide any authorized distributor letters as necessary for non-manufactured items that state you are authorized distributors for Hill AFB, Utah. You are encouraged to provide any documentation to support your business�s capability in meeting the requirements. Failure to provide this type of documentation may result in the Government being unable to adequately assess your business�s capabilities to supply MABSM Sustainment and Implementation services. Questions related to this market survey should be addressed to the contact provided below. The question must contain a phone number and email address for responses. Please provide all responses to this survey � to include any questions or comments you might have � to the requiring activity no later than 08 October 2026 to the attention to Hannah Rearick via email: hannah.rearick@us.af.mil or to Nate Littlewood via email: nathanial.littlewood@us.af.mil. title: Government is conducting market research to identify qualified commercial HVAC contractors.
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify qualified commercial HVAC contractors capable of providing an HVAC solution for an existing facility. The Government's objective is to maximize use of existing building infrastructure where technically feasible rather than perform unnecessary demolition or complete replacement. Interested contractors should have experience evaluating existing HVAC infrastructure and developing retrofit solutions that may incorporate or interface with existing ductwork, electrical systems, controls, structural components, roof/wall penetrations, condensate systems and mechanical spaces. Contractors should be capable of conducting a site survey and recommending a technically acceptable solution that addresses equipment sizing, zoning, energy efficiency, compatibility with existing systems, controls integration, installation requirements and long-term maintainability.

We verwijzen u naar Mercell voor de aanbestedingsleidraad en een wijzigingslog. Dit betreft een Europese aanbesteding voor het sluiten van een raamovereenkomst met één deskundige partner voor de technische ontwikkeling, uitbreiding, integratie, ondersteuning en het beheer van het SAS‑Dataplatform. De opdracht omvat het verder professionaliseren van het dataplatform, het realiseren van veilige en toekomstbestendige koppelingen met diverse bronsystemen, en het ondersteunen van Opdrachtgever in datagedreven werken. De raamovereenkomst heeft een initiële looptijd van drie jaar, met de mogelijkheid tot twee keer één jaar verlenging. Hiermee beoogt WSRL een duurzame samenwerking die bijdraagt aan stabiliteit, schaalbaarheid en doorontwikkeling van het dataplatform. Zie aanbestedingsleidraad voor de inhoudelijke beschrijving. De Algemene waterschapsinkoopvoorwaarden voor diensten (AWVODI-2018) zijn van toepassing. Voorwaarden van de Inschrijver of andere algemene voorwaarden worden uitdrukkelijk van de hand gewezen. De Inschrijver dient zich volledig aan de door Waterschap Rivierenland gestelde voorwaarden te conformeren. Door het doen van een inschrijving gaat de Inschrijver daarmee akkoord.

title: LOP Fire Protection and Unwatering Pump System
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Portland District has a requirement for an open-market, FOB destination supply procurement of a commercial fire protection and unwatering pumping system for Lookout Point Dam in Lane County, Oregon. As part of a planned deep drawdown of the Lookout Point reservoir, the penstock will be dewatered and the plant�s normal service-water supply temporarily removed, disabling transformer cooling and fire protection while primary power is back fed from the transmission line. To sustain fire protection and support unwatering operations during this period, USACE intends to procure new equipment and associated piping, including but not limited to the following: One 650 GPM vertical pump/motor assembly at 200 ft total dynamic head (?50 HP) and one 2000 GPM vertical pump/motor assembly at 51 ft total dynamic head (?20 HP), both water?lubricated vertical line?shaft units designed in accordance with AWWA E103 and HI 9.1�9.5. A complete fire protection pumping package, to include a UL?listed fire pump controller for a 50 HP, 480 VAC motor; a jockey pump system (0.25 HP, nominal 90 psi); a manual transfer switch for dual fire/unwatering service; and new overload protection compatible with an existing 125A Westinghouse AB DE?ION breaker panel. Associated 10?inch and 6?inch Schedule 40 carbon steel piping, flanges, fittings, valves, pressure relief and pressure regulating valves, and accessories in accordance with ASME B16.5/B31.3, AWWA C500/C517/C530, and the applicable ASTM, ANSI, NEMA, NFPA, and UL standards. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 333914 Measuring, Dispensing, and Other Pumping Equipment Manufacturing, with a small business size standard of 750 employees. This procurement is set-aside, 100% for small business concerns. This synopsis is not a request for quotes (RFQ), proposals (RFP), or an invitation for bids (IFB). This is a pre-solicitation notice indicating that a solicitation for a competitive acquisition for the award of one firm-fixed-price contract is intended to be issued via Contract Opportunities at SAM.gov in approximately 1 day or less. This announcement is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, implied or otherwise, to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Quotes will be due approximately 10 days from the date the solicitation is issued, however, the 10-day time frame is estimated and subject to change. The definitive solicitation closing due date and time will be stated in the solicitation once issued and any associated amendments as applicable. All responsible sources may submit a quotation for consideration. Quotations must conform to the specifications provided with the solicitation upon its issuance. For contractors to conduct business with the Department of Defense, the contractor must provide registration information to the System for Award Management (SAM). Pursuant to RFO 4.203-1(b), firms must be SAM registered at the time their quotation is submitted. Registration instructions may be obtained, and online registration may be accomplished, at SAM.gov.

title: Logistic Vehicle System Replacement (LVSR) Training IDIQ
description: Marine Corps Installations East � Regional Contracting Office intends to award a sole-source contract to OSHKOSH DEFENSE, LLC, located at 2307 OREGON ST., OSHKOSH, WI 54902, in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 5.301(a). The requirement is to provide maintenance training on the Logistics Vehicle System Replacement (LVSR) Cargo variant. These services are essential to ensure maintainers can effectively troubleshoot, inspect, and repair the system. The desired outcome is the successful delivery of multiple comprehensive 9-day LVSR Cargo Maintenance courses at MCB Camp Lejeune, NC, blending classroom theory with hands-on practical application. The Contractor shall provide instruction for up to twelve (12) Government personnel per course iteration. For each system covered, the Contractor shall instruct students on component identification, theory of operation, inspection, testing, and fault diagnosis in accordance with the applicable Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) technical manuals. The Period of Performance will be for five (5) years, consisting of a single sixty-month (60-month) ordering period. All training shall be conducted at Government-provided facilities on Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, NC. The IDIQ contract was awarded on 1 September 2026 for a total of $550,640.00.

description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Portland District has a requirement for an FOB destination supply procurement of a commercial 20-ton refrigerated closed-loop water chiller system for a large transformer. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 333415 Air Conditioning and Warm Air Heating Equipment and Commercial and Industrial Refrigeration Equipment Manufacturing, with a small business size standard of 1,250 employees. This announcement is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, implied or otherwise, to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Quotes will be due approximately 10 days from the date the solicitation is issued, however, the 10-day time frame is estimated and subject to change. The definitive solicitation closing due date and time will be stated in the solicitation once issued and any associated amendments as applicable. All responsible sources may submit a quotation for consideration. Quotations must conform to the specifications provided with the solicitation upon its issuance. description: The Army Research Laboratory (ARL) requires Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) supplies and services to sustain, maintain, repair, restore, modify, upgrade, expand, and maintain interoperability of Governmentowned FISICA/L3 Flash X-ray and Computed Radiography (CR) systems. The supplies and services covered by this justification are limited to FISICA Applied Technologies OEM products and services required to support Government-owned FISICA/L3 Flash X-ray and CR systems currently installed or operated by ARL. Covered supplies may include FISICA OEM X-ray tubes of various power ratings; remote and demountable tubeheads and associated cables; control cables; capacitor modules; high-voltage power supplies; X-ray controller (XCON) trigger systems; trigger 3 transformers; charge resistors; OEM components, connectors, and assemblies; CR image plates; image scanners/readers; controller software; and other FISICA OEM components necessary to maintain or support Government-owned FISICA/L3 equipment. Covered services may include factory maintenance and repair; troubleshooting; pulser rebuilding; repair or replacement of high-voltage components; calibration and certification; refurbishment; installation of replacement components; OEM engineering support; and modifications and upgrades to existing Government-owned FISICA/L3 equipment, including power-supply and trigger-system upgrades and air conversion of existing 300 kV and 450 kV Flash X-ray systems.

description: Przedmiotem zamówienia jest świadczenie usług wywozu segregowanych odpadów stałych z nieruchomości Ministerstwa Finansów: 2.1.1 przy ul. Wymagania dotyczące zatrudnienia zostały określone w § 8 PPU. 2.3 Zamawiający przewiduje możliwość wydłużenia okresu realizacji Umowy, z zastosowaniem prawa opcji (dalej zwanego „Opcją”), określonego w § 2 ust. 3 i §13 PPU. Realizacja Opcji zostanie uruchomiona przez Zamawiającego, o ile będzie posiadał środki finansowe i uzasadnioną potrzebę realizacji czynności wchodzących w zakres Opcji. title: Slovakia – Construction work – Zníženie energetickej náročnosti NsP Prievidza so sídlom v Bojniciach" - stavebné práce
description: Stavebné práce sú zamerané na úpravu jednotlivých pavilónov areálu nemocnice s poliklinikou za účelom zníženia energetickej náročnosti a prevádzkovania z hľadiska úspory energií jednotlivých budov. title: Switzerland – Hydro-electric plant construction work – Pumpspeicherwerk Grimsel 4 - Bauhauptlos
description: Das PSW Grimsel 4 nutzt mit zwei Maschinengruppen ohne zusätzlich gefasstes Wasser das vorhandene Potenzial zwischen den beiden bestehenden Speichern Grimsel- und Räterichsbodensee. Auf Grund der kurzen Distanz zwischen den beiden Seen sowie der bereits bestehenden Anlagenteile kann mit dem PSW Grimsel 4 ein wirtschaftlich attraktives Kraftwerk realisiert werden. Neben den erwähnten Stauseen nutzt das Projektvorhaben weitere bestehende Anlagenteile, insbesondere die Erschliessung- und Versorgungsanlagen der bestehenden Kraftwerke an der Grimsel, sowie das bereits im Zusammenhang mit dem Ersatz der Staumauer Spitallamm realisierte Einlaufbauwerk Grimselsee mit Drosselklappenkammer (Vorinvestition Grimsel 4). Die neu zu erstellenden Bauwerke umfassen im Generellen die Weiterführung des oberwasserseitigen Triebwassersystem ab der Drosselklappenkammer mit Flachstrecke und Druckschacht, die Kavernenzentrale, das unterwasserseitige Triebwassersystem mit Unterwasserstollen und Auslaufbauwerk sowie zusätzliche Erschliessungsstollen. Das neue Kraftwerk weist bei einer Ausbauwassermenge von 70 m3/s eine Gesamtleistung von 150 MW auf und schliesst den vorhandenen Engpass im hydraulischen System zwischen Grimsel- und Räterichsbodensee. Daneben dient das Kraftwerk auch der See- und Zuflussbewirtschaftung, wodurch Wasserverluste bei Hochwasser vermieden werden können und ein wesentlicher Beitrag zum Hochwasserschutz geleistet wird. Dank seiner flexiblen Betriebsweise kann das PSW Grimsel 4 sowohl auf kurzfristige Netzschwankungen reagieren als auch im Umwälzbetrieb Lastspitzen abdecken. In Zeiten von Überkapazitäten im Netz kann überschüssige Energie aufgenommen und gespeichert werden. In Bedarfssituationen steht die gespeicherte Energie als Spitzenstrom zur Verfügung. Dadurch unterstützt Grimsel 4 nicht nur die Glättung von Lastprofilen, sondern auch die Stabilisierung von Spannung und Frequenz im Übertragungsnetz. Das PSW Grimsel 4 ist zusätzlich in der Lage, im sogenannten hydraulischen Kurzschluss betrieben zu werden. Dabei wird ein Teil des gepumpten Wassers unmittelbar wieder turbiniert, ohne den Speicherkreislauf vollständig zu durchlaufen. Diese Betriebsweise erlaubt es, sehr schnell auf sich verändernde Netzbedingungen zu reagieren, ohne dabei den Pumpbetrieb unterbrechen zu müssen. Dies erhöht die Reaktionsfähigkeit des Kraftwerks erheblich und macht es zu einem äusserst wertvollen Werkzeug im modernen Netzbetrieb. Neben der Energieproduktion bietet das PSW Grimsel 4 auch Systemdienstleistungen wie Primär-, Sekundär- und Tertiärregelung. Die hohe Flexibilität des Pumpspeicherkraftwerks ermöglicht es, Regelenergie in kürzester Zeit bereitzustellen, was angesichts der zunehmenden Volatilität der Strommärkte einen entscheidenden Vorteil darstellt. Mit diesen Eigenschaften erfüllt das PSW Grimsel 4 eine zentrale Rolle in der Energiewende und trägt wesentlich zur Versorgungssicherheit sowie zur effizienten Nutzung der Wasserkraftressourcen bei. Umfang der Arbeiten / Hauptmengen Die folgenden Bauwerke sind im Rahmen des Bauhauptloses für das PSW Grimsel 4 neu zu erstellen: - Triebwassersystem mit - Restausbruch Oberwasser-Druckstollen Flachstrecke I (ODF I) - Oberwasser-Druckschacht (ODS) - Oberwasser Druckstollen Flachstrecke II (ODF II) - Verteilleitung Oberwasser (VOW) - Verteilleitung Unterwasser (VUW) - Unterwasser-Druckstollen (UDS) - Ein- und Auslaufbauwerk im Räterichsbodensee (ABR), exkl. Voreinschnitt (ETR) - Kavernenzentrale (ZGR4) - Verschiedene Zugangs-, Versorgungs- und baulogistische Stollen Der Triebwasserweg zwischen den beiden Speichern Grimsel- und Räterichsbodensee verläuft gestreckt. Die Trassenlage wurde mit Blick auf eine minimale Länge des Triebwasserwegs optimiert. Die geringe horizontale Gesamtlänge von nur knapp 1.2 km erlaubt es, sowohl im Ober- (OW), als auch im Unterwasser (UW) auf ein Wasserschloss zu verzichten, ohne dabei grössere Betriebseinschränkungen in Kauf nehmen zu müssen.

buyer: Consorci de Salut i d’Atenció Social de Catalunya
title: Spain – Research and experimental development services – Pre-commercial Procurement of an innovative Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations (suHCO)
description: suHCO (Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations) is a European project funded under the Horizon Europe programme (Grant Agreement No. 101226802) and implemented through a Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) scheme. The project aims to support health and care organisations in their transition towards more sustainable and environmentally responsible models by fostering the development of innovative digital solutions. Through the PCP process, suHCO will procure research and development services for the creation of an AI-enabled digital platform capable of helping healthcare organisations assess their sustainability performance, identify improvement opportunities, plan and implement actions, monitor progress, and support evidence-based decision-making. The future solution is expected to integrate sustainability knowledge, regulatory requirements, standards, best practices and relevant data sources, providing users with practical guidance tailored to their organisational context. It should also support sustainable procurement processes, impact assessment, reporting activities and organisational change management. The project is driven by a Buyers Group composed of healthcare organisations from Spain, Italy and Wales. The solutions developed during the PCP will be progressively designed, prototyped and validated in real healthcare environments to ensure their relevance, usability and scalability. By bringing together healthcare providers, technology developers and sustainability experts, suHCO seeks to stimulate innovation and contribute to the sustainability objectives of European health systems.

title: Switzerland – Hydro-electric plant construction work – Pumpspeicherwerk Grimsel 4 - Bauhauptlos
description: Das PSW Grimsel 4 nutzt mit zwei Maschinengruppen ohne zusätzlich gefasstes Wasser das vorhandene Potenzial zwischen den beiden bestehenden Speichern Grimsel- und Räterichsbodensee. Auf Grund der kurzen Distanz zwischen den beiden Seen sowie der bereits bestehenden Anlagenteile kann mit dem PSW Grimsel 4 ein wirtschaftlich attraktives Kraftwerk realisiert werden. Neben den erwähnten Stauseen nutzt das Projektvorhaben weitere bestehende Anlagenteile, insbesondere die Erschliessung- und Versorgungsanlagen der bestehenden Kraftwerke an der Grimsel, sowie das bereits im Zusammenhang mit dem Ersatz der Staumauer Spitallamm realisierte Einlaufbauwerk Grimselsee mit Drosselklappenkammer (Vorinvestition Grimsel 4). Die neu zu erstellenden Bauwerke umfassen im Generellen die Weiterführung des oberwasserseitigen Triebwassersystem ab der Drosselklappenkammer mit Flachstrecke und Druckschacht, die Kavernenzentrale, das unterwasserseitige Triebwassersystem mit Unterwasserstollen und Auslaufbauwerk sowie zusätzliche Erschliessungsstollen. Das neue Kraftwerk weist bei einer Ausbauwassermenge von 70 m3/s eine Gesamtleistung von 150 MW auf und schliesst den vorhandenen Engpass im hydraulischen System zwischen Grimsel- und Räterichsbodensee. Daneben dient das Kraftwerk auch der See- und Zuflussbewirtschaftung, wodurch Wasserverluste bei Hochwasser vermieden werden können und ein wesentlicher Beitrag zum Hochwasserschutz geleistet wird. Dank seiner flexiblen Betriebsweise kann das PSW Grimsel 4 sowohl auf kurzfristige Netzschwankungen reagieren als auch im Umwälzbetrieb Lastspitzen abdecken. In Zeiten von Überkapazitäten im Netz kann überschüssige Energie aufgenommen und gespeichert werden. In Bedarfssituationen steht die gespeicherte Energie als Spitzenstrom zur Verfügung. Dadurch unterstützt Grimsel 4 nicht nur die Glättung von Lastprofilen, sondern auch die Stabilisierung von Spannung und Frequenz im Übertragungsnetz. Das PSW Grimsel 4 ist zusätzlich in der Lage, im sogenannten hydraulischen Kurzschluss betrieben zu werden. Dabei wird ein Teil des gepumpten Wassers unmittelbar wieder turbiniert, ohne den Speicherkreislauf vollständig zu durchlaufen. Diese Betriebsweise erlaubt es, sehr schnell auf sich verändernde Netzbedingungen zu reagieren, ohne dabei den Pumpbetrieb unterbrechen zu müssen. Dies erhöht die Reaktionsfähigkeit des Kraftwerks erheblich und macht es zu einem äusserst wertvollen Werkzeug im modernen Netzbetrieb. Neben der Energieproduktion bietet das PSW Grimsel 4 auch Systemdienstleistungen wie Primär-, Sekundär- und Tertiärregelung. Die hohe Flexibilität des Pumpspeicherkraftwerks ermöglicht es, Regelenergie in kürzester Zeit bereitzustellen, was angesichts der zunehmenden Volatilität der Strommärkte einen entscheidenden Vorteil darstellt. Mit diesen Eigenschaften erfüllt das PSW Grimsel 4 eine zentrale Rolle in der Energiewende und trägt wesentlich zur Versorgungssicherheit sowie zur effizienten Nutzung der Wasserkraftressourcen bei. Umfang der Arbeiten / Hauptmengen Die folgenden Bauwerke sind im Rahmen des Bauhauptloses für das PSW Grimsel 4 neu zu erstellen: - Triebwassersystem mit - Restausbruch Oberwasser-Druckstollen Flachstrecke I (ODF I) - Oberwasser-Druckschacht (ODS) - Oberwasser Druckstollen Flachstrecke II (ODF II) - Verteilleitung Oberwasser (VOW) - Verteilleitung Unterwasser (VUW) - Unterwasser-Druckstollen (UDS) - Ein- und Auslaufbauwerk im Räterichsbodensee (ABR), exkl. Voreinschnitt (ETR) - Kavernenzentrale (ZGR4) - Verschiedene Zugangs-, Versorgungs- und baulogistische Stollen Der Triebwasserweg zwischen den beiden Speichern Grimsel- und Räterichsbodensee verläuft gestreckt. Die Trassenlage wurde mit Blick auf eine minimale Länge des Triebwasserwegs optimiert. Die geringe horizontale Gesamtlänge von nur knapp 1.2 km erlaubt es, sowohl im Ober- (OW), als auch im Unterwasser (UW) auf ein Wasserschloss zu verzichten, ohne dabei grössere Betriebseinschränkungen in Kauf nehmen zu müssen.

title: Switzerland – Archiving services – Zentrale Archivierung für Konkursakten
description: Alle Zürcher Notariate sind gleichzeitig Konkursämter und Grundbuchämter. Zürcher Konkursämter sind verpflichtet, nicht nur die eigenen Akten aus einem Konkursverfahren aufzubewahren, sondern auch die Geschäftsakten der jeweiligen konkursiten Firma. Die gesetzliche Aufbewahrungspflicht beträgt grundsätzlich 10 Jahre (für einzelne Akten 30 Jahre). Insbesondere für die zehnjährige Aufbewahrung der Geschäftsakten betreiben die Notariate heute neun sogenannte Zentralarchive. Die neun Zentralarchive befinden sich an sieben Standorten und sind jeweils einem Konkursamt/Notariat vor Ort angegliedert. Das Management eines Archivs (Lagerinventar, Zu- und Abgänge) erfolgt durch einen Notariats-Mitarbeitenden aus dem Notariat vor Ort. Eine IT-Applikation bietet eine Gesamtübersicht über die Auslastung der einzelnen Archive. Die steigende Zahl von Konkursen im Kanton Zürich führt dazu, dass auch die Menge an Konkurs- und Geschäftsakten ansteigt und die bestehenden Zentralarchive der Notariate die Grenze ihrer Kapazität erreichen, teilweise bereits erreicht haben. Aus diesem Grund und dem Bedürfnis, die Konkursämter des Kantons nicht zusätzlich mit Lagerdienstleistungen zu belasten, hat die Geschäftsleitung des Notariatsinspektorats ein Outsourcing der Konkursaktenlagerung als zukunftsfähige, skalierbare Lösung beschlossen.

description: En vertu de la nouvelle décision relative au réseau routier (NEB), la route du Kandertal reliant Spiez à Kandersteg, a été intégrée au réseau des routes nationales à partir du 01.01.2020. Certains ponts présentant des dégâts importants, les ouvrages les plus menacés feront l’objet de mesures individuelles visant à leur remise en état ou à leur remplacement au cours des six prochaines années. Concrètement, cela comprend la rénovation des ponts K01, K30, K32 et K33, ainsi que la reconstruction des ponts K13 et K25. Le présent appel d’offres porte sur les prestations d’auteur de projet suivi environnemental (APR SER) dans les phases de réalisation (phases SIA 41 à 53) Au cours de ces phases, l’APR SER veuille à ce que le projet soit réalisé dans le respect de la législation en vigueur en matière d’environnement (lois, règlements, directives et recommandations) ainsi que la mise en œuvre des mesures environnementales appropriées. A cet effet, les spécialistes mandatés assument les tâches suivantes : - Planification/Appels d’offres : L’APR SER conseille les planificateurs et le Maître d’Ouvrage lors de l’élaboration du projet d’intervention ainsi que durant les appels d’offres. Il contrôle la planification détaillée des mesures de protection, de remise en état et de remplacement. - Conseil / Coordination : L’APR SER se tient à disposition de la direction des travaux pendant la réalisation pour répondre aux questions relatives à l’environnement et participe selon besoin aux séances de chantier. - Formation / Contrôle : Au début des travaux, l’APR SER soutient la direction des travaux dans la formation des entreprises et ses ouvriers. Il effectue des visites de chantier et vérifie le respect de la législation en matière de protection d’environnement par l’entreprise, la mise en œuvre correcte et complète des mesures de protection, de remise en état et de compensation, ainsi que le respect des mesures figurant sur la liste VAK Environnement (contrôle de l’exécution et des conditions imposées) - Documentation : L’APR SER tient à jour une documentation relatives aux contrôles de chantier sous forme d’un journal de chantier. Il est également responsable pour l’établissement et la mise à jour de la liste VAK environnement. Après la fin de travaux, le PV SER rédige un rapport final SER détaillé.

title: Switzerland – Construction work for bridges – N06.48 MP-190073 - NEB Kandertal EM - Baumeisterarbeiten Brücken K 32 und K 33 (ID 12021)
description: Travaux de génie civil pour la remise en état de deux ponts mixtes en béton armé. Les ponts K32 et K33 sont situés avant Kandersteg et font partie de la route nationale N06 Frutigen – Kandersteg. La N06 est la route d’accès au village de Kandersteg, ainsi qu’au transport autos BLS au Lötschberg. Le trafic sur ces deux ponts varie considérablement et est particulièrement intense par beau temps et pendant la période des vacances. Du côté de Frutigen, l’afflux de véhicule est constant, tandis que celui provenant de Kandersteg se fait par vagues (Transport autos Lötschberg). Construits dans les années 1970, ces deux ponts présentent des dégâts importants et des déficiences statiques. Par conséquent leur utilisation est actuellement restreinte. Seul les véhicules de 20 t maximum peuvent circuler sans restriction. Le point K32 mesure 140 m et comporte quatre travées ; le pont K33 mesure 60 m est comporte deux travées. En coupe transversale, les ponts se compose de deux poutres en acier posées sur des appuis, sur lesquelles repose une dalle en béton. Les piliers et les culées sont constituées de disques en béton armé et reposent sur des fondations superficielles dans les pentes raides de la Kander. Les dégâts et déficiences statiques concernent les deux points, tant au niveau des superstructure que des infrastructures. Des mesures de remise en état et de renforcement de grande envergure sont donc nécessaire.

Swissgrid met à jour périodiquement les données LiDAR et les prises de vues aériennes afin d’identifier les changements dans le périmètre des tracés, d’évaluer les risques d’exploitation liés aux distances entre les lignes et leur environnement, ainsi que d’intégrer dans le jeu de données les nouvelles lignes et les transformations du réseau. Les vols de mesure (acquisition LiDAR et prises de vues aériennes) doivent être réalisés par le Mandataire dans les périmètres définis par Swissgrid et conformément aux spécifications techniques du présent cahier des charges. Les données résultantes servent de base aux évaluations ultérieures dans PLS-CADD. La modélisation et l’analyse dans PLS-CADD ne font pas partie du présent mandat.
